column1: Which of the following is a proper noun?
column2: A proper noun names a specific person or place. 'Delhi' is a specific city name.

column1: What type of noun is 'team' or 'army'?
column2: A collective noun refers to a group of people or things as a single unit.

column1: Which of the following is an abstract noun?
column2: Abstract nouns name ideas or qualities that cannot be seen or touched. 'Freedom' is one such concept.
The word child has an irregular plural form — children — not childs.

column1: Which sentence contains a common noun?
column2: A common noun names any general person, place, or thing — not a specific one.

column1: Which of the following is a material noun?
column2: Material nouns name raw materials or substances from which things are made. Gold is an example.

column1: 'Furniture' is an example of which type of noun?
column2: Furniture is a collective noun used to refer to a group of items used in a room together.

column1: Identify the noun in this sentence: 'The teacher explained the lesson.'
column2: 'Teacher' is a common noun referring to a person. 'Lesson' is also a noun but the question asks you to identify any noun.

column1: Which of the following nouns is both singular and plural?
column2: Sheep does not change its form whether you are referring to one animal or many.

column1: Which of the following is a compound noun?
column2: A compound noun is made up of two or more words that together form a single noun. 'Toothbrush' is a classic example.
